It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–2} Allah, exalted is He, informs us of something that contains the command to glorify the Qur'an and to attend to it: that it is {a revelation from Allah}, the One who is worshipped (al-ma'luh), the Deity; because of the attributes of perfection He possesses and the blessings He alone bestows, the One to whom belong complete might and perfect wisdom.

{3–5} Then He confirmed this by mentioning the signs on the horizons and within the self: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the creatures He scattered in them, the benefits He placed in them, and the water Allah sent down, by which Allah gives life to the lands and the servants. All of these are clear signs and evident proofs of the truthfulness of this great Qur'an and of the soundness of what it contains of wisdom and rulings, and they also point to the perfection of Allah, the Exalted, and to the resurrection and the rising again.

{6–10} Then Allah, exalted is He, divided people, with regard to benefiting from His signs or not, into two categories:
One category derives proof from them, reflects upon them, benefits and is thereby elevated. These are the believers in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day with complete faith, which brought them to the level of certainty. Thus their intellects were purified, and their knowledge, insight and sciences increased through it.
The other category hears the signs of Allah with a hearing by which the proof is established against them, then turns away from them and waxes arrogant, as if they had not heard them, because they did not purify or cleanse their hearts. Rather, because of their arrogance toward them, their transgression increased. And when they know anything of the signs of Allah, they take them in mockery. So Allah, exalted is He, threatened them with woe, saying: {Woe to every sinful liar}; that is, a liar in his speech and a sinner in his deeds. He informed that for them there is a painful punishment, and that {behind them is Hell}, which suffices as their severe punishment, and that {what they earned will not avail them at all}: of wealth, {nor those they took as protectors other than Allah}: whom they sought to help them. They failed them when they most needed them, even had they been of benefit.

{11} Having made clear His Qur'anic and evident signs, and that people are of two categories regarding them, He informed that the Qur'an, which contains these lofty matters, is {guidance}. He said: {This is guidance}. This is a general description of the entire Qur'an, for it guides to the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, through His sacred attributes and praiseworthy acts; it guides to the knowledge of His messengers, their friends and their enemies and their qualities; it guides to righteous deeds and calls to them, and it clarifies evil deeds and forbids them; it guides to the explanation of recompense for deeds and clarifies worldly and otherworldly recompense. So the rightly guided were guided by it and thus prospered and attained happiness. {As for those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord}: the clear and decisive ones, which none disbelieves in except one whose wrongdoing is extreme and whose transgression is multiplied, {for them is a punishment of painful wretchedness (rijz)}.

{1–2} Allah, exalted is He, informs us of something that contains the command to glorify the Qur'an and to attend to it: that it is {a revelation from Allah}, the One who is worshipped (al-ma'luh), the Deity; because of the attributes of perfection He possesses and the blessings He alone bestows, the One to whom belong complete might and perfect wisdom.

{3–5} Then He confirmed this by mentioning the signs on the horizons and within the self: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the creatures He scattered in them, the benefits He placed in them, and the water Allah sent down, by which Allah gives life to the lands and the servants. All of these are clear signs and evident proofs of the truthfulness of this great Qur'an and of the soundness of what it contains of wisdom and rulings, and they also point to the perfection of Allah, the Exalted, and to the resurrection and the rising again.

{6–10} Then Allah, exalted is He, divided people, with regard to benefiting from His signs or not, into two categories:
One category derives proof from them, reflects upon them, benefits and is thereby elevated. These are the believers in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day with complete faith, which brought them to the level of certainty. Thus their intellects were purified, and their knowledge, insight and sciences increased through it.
The other category hears the signs of Allah with a hearing by which the proof is established against them, then turns away from them and waxes arrogant, as if they had not heard them, because they did not purify or cleanse their hearts. Rather, because of their arrogance toward them, their transgression increased. And when they know anything of the signs of Allah, they take them in mockery. So Allah, exalted is He, threatened them with woe, saying: {Woe to every sinful liar}; that is, a liar in his speech and a sinner in his deeds. He informed that for them there is a painful punishment, and that {behind them is Hell}, which suffices as their severe punishment, and that {what they earned will not avail them at all}: of wealth, {nor those they took as protectors other than Allah}: whom they sought to help them. They failed them when they most needed them, even had they been of benefit.

{11} Having made clear His Qur'anic and evident signs, and that people are of two categories regarding them, He informed that the Qur'an, which contains these lofty matters, is {guidance}. He said: {This is guidance}. This is a general description of the entire Qur'an, for it guides to the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, through His sacred attributes and praiseworthy acts; it guides to the knowledge of His messengers, their friends and their enemies and their qualities; it guides to righteous deeds and calls to them, and it clarifies evil deeds and forbids them; it guides to the explanation of recompense for deeds and clarifies worldly and otherworldly recompense. So the rightly guided were guided by it and thus prospered and attained happiness. {As for those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord}: the clear and decisive ones, which none disbelieves in except one whose wrongdoing is extreme and whose transgression is multiplied, {for them is a punishment of painful wretchedness (rijz)}.

{12} He, may He be exalted, informs of His favour upon His servants and His kindness toward them in subjecting the sea for the movement of ships and vessels by His command and facilitation, ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾: through all kinds of trade and gain, ﴿and that perhaps you will be grateful﴾ to God, may He be exalted. For when you give thanks to Him, He increases you in His blessings and rewards you for your gratitude with a great reward.

{13} ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾; that is, from His bounty and kindness. This includes the celestial and terrestrial bodies, and what God has deposited in them: the sun, the moon, the fixed stars and the planets, kinds of animals, varieties of trees and fruits, types of minerals, and other things prepared for the benefit of the children of Adam and for the benefit of what is among their necessities. This obliges them to exert their utmost effort in thanking Him for His blessing, and to let their thoughts penetrate deeply into reflection upon His signs and His wisdom. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾. The sum of the matter is that their creation, their management and their subjection indicate the execution of God's will and the perfection of His power.

What is in them of firm construction, mastery and wondrous craftsmanship, and beauty of form, indicates the perfection of His wisdom and knowledge.

What is in them of vastness, greatness and abundance indicates the breadth of His dominion and authority.

What is in them of particularisation and of opposites indicates that He is the one who does what He wills.

What is in them of benefits and interests, religious and worldly, indicates the breadth of His mercy, the comprehensiveness of His bounty and kindness, and the subtlety of His gentleness and goodness. All of this indicates that He alone is the one worshipped, the deity to whom worship, humility and love are fitting only, and that His messengers are truthful in what they brought. These are clear rational proofs that admit of no doubt or uncertainty.

{16} That is: We bestowed upon the Children of Israel blessings that were not granted to any other people, and We gave them {the Book}; that is, the Torah, the Gospel, judgment among people, and the prophethood, by which they were distinguished. Prophethood came to be among the descendants of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), most of whom were from the Children of Israel. {And We provided for them of the good things}: of food, drink and clothing, and the sending down of the manna and quails upon them. {And We preferred them over the worlds}; that is, over the creation, by these blessings. This literal generality excludes this Ummah, for they are "the best Ummah ever brought forth for mankind" (Q. 3:110), and the context indicates that what is meant is other than this Ummah, since Allah is recounting to us what He bestowed upon the Children of Israel and the distinction He gave them over others.

Also, the virtues by which the Children of Israel excelled, such as the Book, judgment, prophethood and other attributes, have all been attained by this Ummah, and this Ummah has been granted many additional virtues beyond them. This Shari'ah is a part of the Shari'ah of the Children of Israel, for this Book is a guardian (muhayymin) over all the earlier books, and Muhammad (ﷺ) confirms all the messengers.

{17} {And We gave them}; that is, We gave the Children of Israel {clear proofs}; that is, indications that distinguish truth from falsehood {concerning the matter}: the decreed matter which Allah conveyed to them. Those signs are the miracles they witnessed at the hand of Musa (peace be upon him). These blessings with which Allah favored the Children of Israel required that they uphold them in the most perfect manner and that they unite upon the truth which Allah made clear to them. But the matter was reversed: they dealt with them contrary to what was required, and they divided over that which they were commanded to unite upon. Therefore He said: {And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them}; that is, the knowledge which necessitates the absence of disagreement. What drove them to disagreement was the transgression (baghy) of some of them against others and injustice. {Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ}: He will distinguish the one who is right from the one who is wrong, and what led them to disagreement was desire or something else.

{20} "This" — the noble Qur'an and the wise Reminder — "is insights (basa'ir) for mankind": that is, through it there is attained clear perception in all matters for mankind, so that benefit is attained through it by the believers. "And" guidance and mercy "for a people who are certain" (yuqinun): they are guided by it to the straight path in the foundations of the religion and its branches, and through it there is attained goodness, joy and happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and that is mercy. Their souls are purified by it, their minds are increased by it, their faith and certainty are augmented by it, and by it the proof is established against whoever persists in obstinacy and opposition.

{21} That is: Do those who do evil, who commit many sins and fall short in their duties to their Lord, think that We will treat them the same as those who believe and do righteous deeds, who fulfill their duties to their Lord, avoid what displeases Him, and always prefer His pleasure over the desires of their own souls? In other words, do they think they will be {equal} in this world and the Hereafter? How evil is what they assume and reckon, and how evil is the judgment they pass! For it is a judgment that contradicts the wisdom of the Wisest of judges and the Best of the just, that conflicts with sound minds and upright natural dispositions, and that opposes what the Books have revealed and the Messengers have reported. Rather, the established and certain judgment is that the believers who do righteous deeds will have victory, success, happiness, and reward in the immediate and the future, each according to the measure of his goodness; and that the evildoers will have wrath, humiliation, punishment, and misery in this world and the Hereafter.

{22} That is: Allah created the heavens and the earth with wisdom, and so that He alone be worshipped, with no partner for Him; then He will recompense, after that, those He commanded to worship Him and bestowed upon them blessings, both apparent and hidden. Did they thank Allah, the Exalted, and carry out what they were commanded? Or did they disbelieve and thereby deserve the recompense of the ungrateful?

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 45, verses 23–26:

{23} God, exalted is He, says: {Have you seen} the misguided man who {has taken his desire as his god}, so he follows whatever his desire inclines him to, whether it pleases God or angers Him. {And God has sent him astray knowing} that guidance is not befitting him and that he will not thrive upon it. {And has sealed his hearing} so he does not hear what benefits him, {and his heart} so he does not comprehend good, {and placed over his sight a covering} that prevents him from looking at the truth. {Then who can guide him after God?} That is, no one can guide him, for God has closed the doors of guidance to him and opened to him the doors of misguidance. God did not wrong him, but he wronged himself and caused the withholding of God's mercy from himself. {Will you not then take heed?} Will you not remember what benefits you so that you follow it, and what harms you so that you avoid it?

{24} {And they say}, that is, those who deny the Resurrection: {There is nothing but our life of this world. We die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time}. That is, it is merely customs and the continuous passing of the cycles of night and day: people die and people live, and no one has returned from death, so there is no return to God and no recompense for their deeds. This statement of theirs proceeds from no knowledge: {They have no knowledge of it; they only conjecture}. Thus they denied the Hereafter and rejected the truthful messengers without any proof that guided them or any evidence, and their claims are nothing but conjectures and assumptions devoid of reality.

{25} For this reason God, exalted is He, says: {And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring back our fathers, if you are truthful."} This is audacity on their part toward God, for they proposed this suggestion and claimed that the truthfulness of God's messengers depends on bringing back their fathers, and that even if they were brought every sign, they would not believe, unless the messengers followed them in what they said. They were liars in what they said; their real aim was to repel the call of the messengers, not to make the truth clear.

{26} God says: {Say, "God gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt," but most people do not know}. And had the knowledge of the Last Day reached their hearts, they would have performed deeds for it and prepared themselves for it.

**Ibn Sa'di, *Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman*, on Surah al-Jathiyah (45), verses 27–37**

{27} God, exalted is He, informs us of the vastness of His dominion and of His sole authority over disposing and governing at all times, and that ﴿on the Day the Hour is established﴾, He will gather all creation for the standing of the Resurrection. Loss will befall the falsifiers, who brought falsehood in order to refute the truth. Their deeds were void, because they were tied to falsehood, so they came to nothing on the Day of Resurrection, the day on which realities become clear. They were rendered powerless, the reward escaped them, and they incurred painful punishment.

{28} Then God described the severity and terror of the Day of Resurrection, so that His servants might be wary of it and His worshippers might prepare for it. He said: ﴿And you will see﴾, O you who witness that Day, ﴿every nation kneeling﴾, upon their knees, out of fear, dread, and awaiting the judgment of the Sovereign, the Most Merciful. ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾, that is, to the law (shari'ah) of their prophet who came to them from God, and whether they upheld it, so that reward and salvation accrue to them, or neglected it, so that loss accrues to them. So the nation of Moses are called to the law of Moses, the nation of Jesus likewise, the nation of Muhammad likewise, and so with others: every nation is called to the law it was charged with. This is one of the possible meanings of the verse, and it is a correct meaning in itself, not open to doubt.

It is also possible that the intended meaning of His words ﴿every nation will be called to its record﴾ is: to the book of their deeds and what was inscribed in it of good and evil, and that each person will be recompensed for what he himself did, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾.

It is also possible that both meanings are intended by the verse.

{29} This is indicated by His saying: ﴿This is Our record; it speaks against you with truth﴾, that is, this Our Book which We sent down to you will judge between you with the truth, which is justice. ﴿Indeed, We were having your deeds transcribed﴾: this is the book of deeds.

{30} For this reason He detailed what He will do with the two groups. He said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, with sound faith, and they confirmed their faith by righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended, ﴿their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, which is the Garden, and what is in it of lasting bliss and sound living. ﴿That is the great attainment﴾, that is, the triumph, the salvation, the profit, and the clear and manifest success, which, when a servant attains it, he attains every good and every evil is repelled from him.

{31} ﴿And as for those who disbelieved﴾ in God, it will be said to them, in rebuke and reproach: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you?﴾, which had guided you to what was good for you and forbade you what was harmful to you, and which are the greatest blessing that reached you had you been granted success in them. But you were arrogant toward them, turned away, and disbelieved in them. So you committed the greatest crime and the gravest sin. ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

{32} They are also rebuked by His saying: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said﴾, denying that: ﴿"We do not know what the Hour is; we think it is only a supposition, and we are not certain."﴾ This was their state in the world, and their attitude toward the resurrection was denial, and they rejected the word of the one who brought it.

{33} He said: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did﴾, that is, there will become manifest to them on the Day of Resurrection the punishments for their deeds. ﴿And there will befall them﴾, that is, there will descend upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾, that is, the punishment they used to mock in the world, both its occurrence and the one who brought it.

He said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, with sound faith, and they confirmed their faith by righteous deeds, both obligatory and recommended, ﴿their Lord will admit them into His mercy﴾, which is the Garden, and what is in it of lasting bliss and sound living. ﴿That is the great attainment﴾, that is, the triumph, the salvation, the profit, and the clear and manifest success, which, when a servant attains it, he attains every good and every evil is repelled from him.

{31} ﴿And as for those who disbelieved﴾ in God, it will be said to them, in rebuke and reproach: ﴿Were not My verses recited to you?﴾, which had guided you to what was good for you and forbade you what was harmful to you, and which are the greatest blessing that reached you had you been granted success in them. But you were arrogant toward them, turned away, and disbelieved in them. So you committed the greatest crime and the gravest sin. ﴿Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

{32} They are also rebuked by His saying: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true and the Hour, there is no doubt about it," you said﴾, denying that: ﴿"We do not know what the Hour is; we think it is only a supposition, and we are not certain."﴾ This was their state in the world, and their attitude toward the resurrection was denial, and they rejected the word of the one who brought it.

{33} He said: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did﴾, that is, there will become manifest to them on the Day of Resurrection the punishments for their deeds. ﴿And there will befall them﴾, that is, there will descend upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾, that is, the punishment they used to mock in the world, both its occurrence and the one who brought it.

{34} ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day"﴾, that is, We will leave you in punishment, for recompense is of the same kind as the deed. ﴿And your refuge is the Fire﴾, that is, it is your abode and your destination. ﴿And for you there are no helpers﴾ who could defend you from the punishment of God or repel His retribution from you.

{35} ﴿That﴾, which has befallen you of punishment, is ﴿because you took the verses of God in mockery﴾, although they call for earnestness and striving and for receiving them with joy, gladness, and delight, ﴿and the worldly life deceived you﴾ with its adornments, pleasures, and desires, so you were content with it, worked for it, and abandoned work for the everlasting abode. ﴿So today they will not be brought out from it, nor will they be granted any leniency﴾, that is, they will not be given respite or returned to the world to do righteous deeds.

{36} ﴿So to God belongs all praise﴾, as befits the majesty of His countenance and the greatness of His sovereignty, ﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾. That is, to Him belongs praise for His lordship over all creation, in that He created them, nurtured them, and bestowed upon them blessings, both outward and inward.

{37} ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, to Him belong majesty, greatness, and glory. Praise contains extolling God with the attributes of perfection and loving and honoring Him, and grandeur contains His magnificence and majesty. Worship is founded on two pillars: love of God and humility before Him, and both arise from knowledge of God's praiseworthy attributes, His majesty, and His greatness. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, who overpowers everything, ﴿the Wise﴾, who places things in their proper places, so He does not legislate except for a wise purpose and benefit, and He does not create except for a useful end and benefit.

The commentary of Surah al-Jathiyah is complete. To God belong praise, gratitude, and grace.
